newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit breaks through 2.52 barrier on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit breaks through 2.52 barrier on rumours.

text.p: The ringgit broke through the psychological 2.52/dollar barrier on a rumour that the U.S. is seeking sanctions against Malaysia's national oil company, Petronas, for involvement in an Iranian project, dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5210/20 a dollar against 2.5135/45 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
The dealers said another rumour that Bank Negara was comfortable with the ringgit being between 2.52 and 2.53 had also triggered fresh sales of the Malaysian unit.
"These are rumours, just being used to sell ringgit down," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore.
"Added to the sanctions report are the rumours that Bank Negara is comfortable with a decline to 2.52 to 2.53 a dollar level," the dealer said.
"This latest talk (of sanctions) hit a market already keen on selling the ringgit which exaggerated the reaction," research firm I.D.E.A. said in a comment.
Neither Petronas nor Bank Negara officials were immediately available for comment.
Ringgit has been declining on dollar shortcovering and selling against the Singapore dollar since late Tuesday.
